Context/Background:
Intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPNs),  including intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasms (IOPNs), and intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasms (ITPNs), are clinically detectable macroscopic non-invasive cyst-forming lesions, some of which progress to invasive pancreatic cancer. Proteins and glycoproteins have proven to be useful clinical biomarkers for classifying cyst-forming neoplasms in the pancreas.Here, we used proteomics and glycoproteomics to characterize a series of histologically and genetically well-characterized surgically resected IPNs, including IPMNs and IOPNs.

Our analysis included 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs and 5 IOPNs), 76 macro-dissected grossly normal duct tissues (NDs, with 32 of the 76 NDs coming from the same resection specimens as the IPNs), and 32 cyst fluid samples (22 from matched IPMN patients, 3 matched IOPN patients, 2 from unrelated IPMN patients, and 5 other cysts).
Prompt: Look at the differential genes between high and low grade IPMN and between high grade IPMN and ND. From the commonly upregulated proteins, nominate a few important genes that are related to Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC) in the literature.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
The dataset “Wang_2025_Cancer_Cell_TableS2M.csv” reports protein fold‐changes and FDRs for two contrasts: high‐grade (HG) vs low‐grade (LG) IPMN, and HG IPMN vs normal duct (ND). Of 7,624 quantified proteins, 279 showed significant (FDR < 0.05) and positive fold‐changes in both contrasts (HG > LG and HG > ND). No raw counts or mutational data are specified; only proteomic comparisons are provided.

Keywords  
IPMN progression; proteomics; glycoproteomics; PDAC; cell‐cycle

Candidate Genes  
MCM3, MCM7, TFRC, LGALS9, HMGB3, SPINT2

0b) Dataset Interrogation of Candidate Genes  
– csv_select: kept all five columns (Gene, HG vs LG IPMN, FDR, HG IPMN vs ND, FDR.1).  
– csv_filter: extracted the six candidate genes from the full table.  
  • All six are present, upregulated in both contrasts, and meet FDR < 0.05.

Nomination of PDAC-Relevant Genes  
From the 279 commonly upregulated proteins, we nominate six proteins with strong literature links to PDAC:  

1. MCM7  
   – HG vs LG IPMN log₂FC 0.905 (FDR 7.8×10⁻³), HG IPMN vs ND log₂FC 0.889 (FDR 6.8×10⁻⁶)  
   – MCM7 is part of the minichromosome maintenance complex, overexpressed in PDAC and linked to tumor proliferation.

2. MCM3  
   – HG vs LG IPMN log₂FC 0.798 (FDR 6.1×10⁻³), HG IPMN vs ND log₂FC 0.802 (FDR 2.4×10⁻⁵)  
   – Also a DNA‐replication licensing factor; high MCM3 levels correlate with poor PDAC prognosis.

3. TFRC (Transferrin Receptor)  
   – HG vs LG IPMN log₂FC 0.665 (FDR 1.2×10⁻²), HG IPMN vs ND log₂FC 1.039 (FDR 4.1×10⁻⁹)  
   – TFRC is upregulated in PDAC cells to support iron uptake and proliferation.

4. LGALS9 (Galectin-9)  
   – HG vs LG IPMN log₂FC 0.718 (FDR 3.9×10⁻³), HG IPMN vs ND log₂FC 0.983 (FDR 5.8×10⁻⁷)  
   – Galectin-9 promotes immune‐evasion in PDAC tumor microenvironment.

5. HMGB3  
   – HG vs LG IPMN log₂FC 0.681 (FDR 6.8×10⁻³), HG IPMN vs ND log₂FC 1.085 (FDR 1.4×10⁻⁸)  
   – A chromatin‐binding protein; HMGB3 drives PDAC cell migration and chemoresistance.

6. SPINT2  
   – HG vs LG IPMN log₂FC 0.949 (FDR 1.9×10⁻²), HG IPMN vs ND log₂FC 1.039 (FDR 2.3×10⁻⁶)  
   – A serine‐protease inhibitor whose loss is associated with PDAC invasion and metastasis.

Next Steps & Clarifications  
1. Validate expression of nominated proteins in independent PDAC cohorts (IHC or targeted proteomics).  
2. Correlate MCM3/7 and TFRC levels with clinical outcomes in invasive PDAC samples.  
3. Functionally test SPINT2 and LGALS9 in PDAC cell‐line models to assess effects on invasion and immune modulation.  
4. Examine whether glycosylation status (glycoproteomics) further stratifies HG IPMN risk markers among these candidates.
